coaching.summary: The brief frames the acquisition as an obvious win, but several important factors are underweighted: integration risk, cultural fit, and the opportunity cost of the 50M outlay. The model treats the synergy estimate (20M+ year one) as a single point — it should be a range so downside scenarios surface. Consider also: would a smaller stake or earn-out reduce execution risk while preserving upside?

strengthen_items.label: Replace point estimate of synergies with a range
strengthen_items.detail: The current synergy estimate of 20M is a single number. Add a low/high range (e.g. 5M floor, 30M ceiling) so the analysis can quantify how much of the deal economics depend on the optimistic case.

strengthen_items.label: Add a do-nothing comparator
strengthen_items.detail: Without a status-quo option, the analysis cannot show whether the deal beats simply continuing organic growth. Add a baseline option that captures revenue trajectory without the acquisition.

elements_considered_but_excluded: The brief mentions cultural fit concerns but no quantified integration cost. Adding this factor lets the analysis express the downside the team raised.
Capital deployed on the acquisition cannot be deployed on organic R&D or buybacks. Surfacing this factor lets the model compare returns across uses.

bias_signals.detail: Brief frames the deal as obviously good (CEO excited, board approved, plenty of cash, huge synergies). Concerns from the team are acknowledged then dismissed.
